title: Max Verstappen branded 'imperious' as comfortable prediction made
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has been branded "imperious" by Karun Chandhok, with the pundit backing the Red Bull driver to seal second in the drivers' championship after a dominant win in Singapore.

Verstappen converted pole position into a lights-to-flag victory at Marina Bay, crossing the line 7.335 seconds clear of Charles Leclerc with Kimi Antonelli completing the podium.

It was the Dutchman's second win of the season and moved him to 221 points, just 17 behind Russell in the standings battle for runner-up spot behind championship leader Antonelli.

Speaking on the Sky F1 podcast, Chandhok said Verstappen's current run of form makes him the clear favourite to finish second overall, pointing to the gap he has closed on Russell in recent rounds.

"He's on imperious form, isn't he? The last few weekends, he's only 17 points off George," Chandhok said. "So, if you're a betting man today, you would put money on Max being second in the world championship.

"The run of form he's on! I just thought he was on such good form, at one with the car, and he didn't overdrive it. That was the key.

"There were so many drivers who could have, would have, should have out-qualified him in the Friday Sprint qualifying and Grand Prix qualifying, and they all made a mistake or didn't put the lap together when it got to the final part of the lap.

"And Max is the one who realised, 'You know what? When we get to the last sector, the grip's not there. I'm just going to not over-attack the entry of 16.' And he did it, and that was the key."

Final Verstappen-Lambiase podium celebration?

Verstappen's race engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, joined him on the podium after the win, a moment Chandhok highlighted given the pair's impending split.

Red Bull confirmed earlier this year that Lambiase will leave to become McLaren's chief racing officer, with Tom Hart already being eased into the role on Verstappen's radio ahead of a full-time takeover in 2027.

Chandhok suggested the Singapore podium could prove to be one of the last shared celebrations between driver and engineer.

"It was great to see GP on the podium with him as well, because of the relationship between them," added Chandhok.

"We don't know if GP will get another chance to be on the podium. We believe he's going to be on gardening leave on 31 December.

"So, who knows if he wins any more races? If they don't, it was nice to see him."

title: Lewis Hamilton spies Ferrari area which could bring 'huge performance' boost
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari could unlock a "huge amount of performance" if the team were better able to understand the Pirelli tyres in F1.

Whilst mastering tyres has always been a complicated matter in F1, in 2026, the art is particularly difficult to master given the high tyre pressures Pirelli has mandated.

Owing to the new straight-line mode in 2026, tyres pressures, especially at the rear at been raised to protect the tyres in case of a straight mode failure and the active aero not opening.

It is as a safety measure as the cars have been designed around lower downforce on the straights with the wings open, with the machines already exceeding the load expectations of Pirelli when the tyres were being designed.

This had led to claims of the tyres feeling like "balloons" - and means that tyre wear and degradation has not been as important a factor as in recent years, with the soft tyres proving to be the overwhelmingly best race tyre in recent races in Azerbaijan and Singapore.

Analysing the point, Hamilton felt that the area of tyre science had a lot of untapped potential for the Scuderia.

"I think when people are watching, they probably don't think too much in-depth about the tyres," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"I think the tyres are the things which deliver a huge amount of performance if you get them working properly.

"And believe it or not, that's a science in itself, so it is an area we could do better.

"I think it could deliver quite a bit of performance."

[Article continues below].

'Easier said than done'

Hamilton also pinpointed that Ferrari needed to sharpen its race weekend execution, but conceded it was 'easier said than done.'

"We're happy with where the car is in terms of where we've developed it," he added.

"We just need a clean weekend and that's all about flowing from the get-go and building up that confidence within ourselves and within the car and then executing.

"It is a lot easier said than done, but we're working on trying to do a better job."

excerpt:
Verstappen Racing seemed on track for a strong result in the GTWC race at Portimão, until a costly mistake earned the car a penalty, before Max Verstappen rallied late on.

After an hour and a half, it was clear that Verstappen Racing, in the #3 Mercedes-AMG GT3, had a shot at finishing on the podium at Portimão. Ben Barnicoat drove a rock-solid first stint and climbed from P13 to P8, after which Chris Lulham immediately showed just how fast he is in this car by moving up to P6. In the laps that followed, he steadily chipped away at his deficit to the leader, the #17 Mercedes with Ralf Aron behind the wheel.

Max Verstappen rallied from a drive-through penalty for the #3 Mercedes-AMG GT3 in the GT race at Portimao to finish in a strong ninth place.

90 minutes into the three-hour race in Portugual, Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham had got the car up to sixth, with the #17 Mercedes of Ralf Aron leading.

While Lulham was working to close the gap, a full-course yellow was called, which would later turn into a safety car. This brought the field back together, and Lulham seemed poised to overtake the #48 Mercedes in the battle for P5, but his first attempt at a pass went wrong.

Lulham made contact with the #48 Mercedes, causing the latter to spin. The #3 Mercedes was able to continue without too much damage, but the obvious problem was almost impossible to ignore: there was a good chance the team would face a penalty.

Ultimately, a drive-through penalty was issued, which Lulham served before the end of his stint, before handing over to Verstappen for the final stint under the lights.

title: Liam Lawson wary of major F1 rival threat as Racing Bulls steal advantage
excerpt:
Liam Lawson is wary of Alpine suddenly stealing away Racing Bulls' fifth place in the constructors' championship, pointing to 2024 as his evidence.

After the Singapore round, Racing Bulls have 100 points in the constructors' standings, 32 ahead of nearest rival Alpine, aided in part by Lawson's standout weekend in Singapore, where he banked fifth in the Sprint and seventh in the grand prix for 10 points overall.

This, coupled with a third successive blank for Alpine, means Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are closing in on securing fifth place for the team, which would be the team's best-ever result in the constructors', and eclipse anything predecessors Toro Rosso or AlphaTauri achieved.

However, despite moving 32 points clear of Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, Lawson was still wary of the threat posed by Alpine - and pointed to the 2024 Sao Paulo GP where Alpine scored a double podium to rocket up the standings.

"Not secure, no," Lawson told media, including RacingNews365 of Racing Bulls' fifth-place after the Singapore weekend.

"We're definitely in a better place, and we've managed to extend the [points lead] over the last few weekends, and [Singapore] for us was a 10-point weekend.

"So it was good and they didn't score in either race, and I'm not even sure they scored in the triple-header, and they've had a very, very fast car.

"I'm happy with the team, and we've made all the right decisions ultimately through these last few weeks, but it is not secure for the rest of the year.

"A couple of years ago, Alpine had a double podium in Brazil, so anything can happen."

[Article continues below].

Alpine's double podium

Prior to the 2024 Sao Paulo GP, Alpine was a lowly ninth in the constructors' standings on just 14 points following a poor season.

It was behind Haas on 46 points, Racing Bulls itself on 36 and Williams on 17.

However, Gasly scored two points in the Sprint before the team struck gold in the torrentially wet race, with Esteban Ocon finishing second and Gasly taking third place.

This haul of 35 points in total rocketed Alpine up the standings to sixth place with 49 points, overhauling all three teams immediately ahead of it.

In the final standings, this haul ensured the team finished above both Racing Bulls and Williams, with Alpine eventually just seven points clear of Haas - with the sixth-place finish worth millions of dollars in extra prize money for the Enstone squad.

title: Rafael Camara reveals F1 race number after Haas signing announcement
excerpt:
Rafael Camara has revealed which F1 race number he is going to use after news of his promotion to grand prix racing with Haas was confirmed.

The Brazilian was confirmed earlier this week as a full-time race driver with the team from the 2027 season, and will replace Esteban Ocon who is departing after two seasons.

Whilst his team-mate is not yet officially confirmed, Oliver Bearman is expected to stay for a third season, with Camara, who is leading the FIA F2 standings, confirming which number he will run on his first Haas F1 car.

Camara will use #50 when he debuts in the Bahrain Grand Prix in March, becoming the first driver to opt to choose the number as their personal pick.

Interestingly, the #50 was used by Bearman himself during his two substitute appearances for Haas in 2024 in Azerbaijan and Sao Paulo, deputising for the banned and then ill, respectively, Kevin Magnussen.

But as Bearman was only a substitute driver, the #50 was then Haas's reverse number and not Bearman's personal choice, which turned out to be #87 when he debuted full-time in 2025.

The article continues below.

Camara explains his choice

When asked by media, including RacingNews365 why he had opted to chose #50, Camara explained his choice.

"We'll be using the #50," he said.

"Obviously the first choice would be #5, but Gabriel [Bortoleto] is using that, but it will be #50 as my birthday is 05/05/2005, and I spoke with my dad, and he said that I'm 50.

"It makes sense with the birthday date, so I'll be using that one for next year."

With the news of Camara's announcement, it leaves just five seats to be publicly announced for the 2027 grid.

These are at Mercedes, where is is unthinkable that either George Russell or world champion-elect Kimi Antonelli will be dropped, at Racing Bulls where Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are hoping they aren't dropped for Camara's F2 rival Nikola Tsolov and the second Haas seat, which is expected to be Bearman's once again.

For Lando Norris, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, and Lewis Hamilton, as they are all still mathematically in title contention, they could all still win and elect to change to the #1 in 2027 - although Hamilton did not do this when winning titles at Mercedes, staying with his #44.

In the case of the reigning champion Norris, he will revert to his previous race number of #4 for 2027, having lost the right to carry the #1, barring an extraordinary comeback.
